key_insight: The sign of a sizable second Josephson harmonic guides two superconducting qutrit designs that strongly suppress relaxation but remain limited by dephasing.
engineering_relevance: Three-junction loops could encode three-level quantum states with noise protection tailored to junction materials and harmonic sign.
method: Use a positive second harmonic and slight junction asymmetry for a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit.
Use a negative second harmonic with weak symmetry breaking, such as a Josephson diode effect, for an alternative protected qutrit.
Microscopically model altermagnetic junctions to investigate gate-controlled harmonic sign.
evidence_signal: Theoretical and microscopic calculations predict an exact charge selection rule for the positive-harmonic design and near-insensitivity to charge noise with correctable quasiparticle errors for the negative-harmonic design.
watch_item: Both designs require a sizable second harmonic, and gate-voltage noise becomes the leading dephasing source in the modeled gate-tunable platform.
paper_title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
